newsitem.title: USA: NY Senate again passes energy bills.
newsitem.headline: NY Senate again passes energy bills.

text.p: The New York Senate has again passed, with technical changes, legislation approved in June designed to lower the cost of electricity and encourage private sector job creation and retention, a Senate spokesman said Wednesday.
The bills approved Tuesday were submitted by Republican Governor Pataki, Senate Majority Leader Joseph L. Bruno said.
One bill (S.7979), entitled the "Power For Prosperity" bill, would make 400 megawatts of low cost power available for economic development.
The "Electric Ratepayer Relief Act" (S.7978) would give utilities better access to lower cost financing.
As a precondition for using this financing mechanism, the New York State Public Service Commission must determine that substantial ratepayer savings would be achieved.
Neither bill has been acted on the the Democrat-controlled Assembly, which has passed energy legislation ignored by the Republic-controlled Senate.
With the end of the legislature's special session, the spokesman said, both bills will die. They will have to be reintroduced next year for further consideration.
